subject: Infra decisioning & PoC next steps — hosting vs dedicated vs private VPC
content:
Message 1/5
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@medsys.ai>, Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.g@medsys.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Infra decisioning & PoC next steps — hosting vs dedicated vs private VPC

Thanks for the time today — quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Workload: low-latency text generation integrated into their clinician UI, peak concurrent users ~120, avg request size ~600 tokens.
- Data sensitivity: PHI will be in prompts; customer requires audit logs, KMS integration, and SOC2 evidence.
- Preferences: Ops wants to avoid on-prem complexity but Security is nervous about multi-tenant hosted.

Options we discussed:
1) Hosted API (fastest onboarding, usage-based) — good for early CA proof; needs contractual SOC2/KMS assurances.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) — predictable throughput, stronger isolation, Redwood-managed infra.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — maximum control, longer lead time and higher cost.

Proposed PoC approach:
- Goal: validate latency SLOs and data controls in a 4-week sprint.
- Criteria: 99th-pct latency < 300ms, KV cache hit > 25%, audit log visibility and KMS test.
- Stakeholders: Rajesh (CTO) — tech signoff, Elena (Product) — UX acceptance, Procurement for T&Cs.

Action items I propose:
- You confirm preferred deployment mode (hosted / dedicated / private) — this drives PoC infra and timelines.
- Marcus to send a concise technical checklist and preliminary sizing for the chosen mode.
- We’ll circulate an initial PoC scope doc and SOC2 evidence pack (attached).

Attachments: rwi_poc_scope_v1.pdf (stub), security_questions_filled.docx (stub)

Thanks — I’ll stand by to align the team once you pick the preferred mode.

Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com

Message 2/5
From: Elena Park <elena.park@medsys.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.g@medsys.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Infra decisioning & PoC next steps — hosting vs dedicated vs private VPC

Appreciate the clear recap, Sergio.

A few notes from our side after internal sync: we’re leaning toward Dedicated capacity as the primary PoC track — tradeoff between faster delivery and stronger isolation. Security will still want to validate KMS flow and logs, but Dedicated removes the multi-tenant concern.

Questions:
- Can Dedicated support customer-managed KMS or at least a bring-your-key option?
- What is the expected lead time to provision dedicated pool for a 4-week PoC (non-prod)?
- Cost estimate for a 4-week reservation vs hosted metered run for the same throughput.

We’ll confirm final decision with Procurement early next week. For now, please proceed with a technical checklist tailored to Dedicated.

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Product | Medsys
elena.park@medsys.ai

Message 3/5
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@medsys.ai>, Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.g@medsys.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T09:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Infra decisioning & PoC next steps — Dedicated checklist and sizing

Thanks Elena — I’ll focus the checklist on Dedicated capacity. High-level notes and a few requests so we can size / timeline accurately: 

Technical checklist (short):
- Expected peak concurrent requests & typical tokens per request (you gave 120 / 600) — confirm burst multiplier (x2?).
- Are there any model variants: small (7B) for retrieval vs large (70B) for summaries? Which models do you want to test in PoC?
- Network: will traffic route through your VPC via peering / Transit? If so, do you have firewall rules we should be aware of?
- KMS: confirm whether a customer-managed key is required or we can integrate with your KMS via cross-account role.
- Data retention: confirm logs retention window for PoC (we can toggle).

Prelim sizing assumptions I’ll use unless you ask otherwise: 2 dedicated GPU nodes (A100 equivalent), short-lived autoscaling for bursts, caching enabled. Provisioning lead time: typically 5–7 business days after contract and PO for non-prod PoC.

I’ll attach a short spreadsheet with request fields (attachment: rwi_poc_sizing_sheet.xlsx). Please fill and return; I’ll iterate with infra.

— Marcus
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Message 4/5
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@medsys.ai>, Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.g@medsys.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Infra decisioning & PoC next steps — Success criteria and timeline

Hi team — adding PoC success criteria and a suggested 4-week timeline so expectations are aligned.

Success criteria (must pass):
- Latency: 99th-pct < 300ms for API calls under expected load.
- Accuracy: sample evaluation set (n=400) meets UX thresholds as defined by Elena (recall/precision baselines attached in scope doc).
- Security: KMS integration tested, access logs available in console, SOC2 evidence pack provided.
- Reliability: <1% failed requests during test windows; automatic fallbacks validate.

Suggested timeline (4 weeks):
Week 0: Contract/PO + infra provisioning (Dedicated non-prod).
Week 1: Model onboarding, basic latency checks, KV cache tuning.
Week 2: End-to-end integration with clinician UI + security tests (KMS + logs).
Week 3: UX evaluation and performance tuning; consolidate results and handoff.

Deliverables: PoC report, runbook for production rollout (if go), and an itemized cost estimate for sustained Dedicated capacity.

If that looks good I’ll prepare the acceptance checklist we can sign off on.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

Message 5/5
From: Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.g@medsys.ai>

Date: 2026-11-11T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Infra decisioning & PoC next steps — confirmation and procurement ask

Thanks everyone — confirming we want to proceed with Dedicated capacity for the PoC. Procurement will review the short contract and PO; I expect sign-off by next Wednesday.

Two final asks before provisioning:
1) Please confirm whether we can use our own KMS key (we prefer BYOK).
2) Share an itemized 4-week cost comparison: Dedicated reserved vs hosted metered for the same throughput.

Procurement will push any contract redlines to procurement@medsys.ai (cc’d). Also, please send a short link to the SOC2 evidence and the PoC scope doc in Drive.

Rajesh Gupta
CTO | Medsys
rajesh.g@medsys.ai

Additional notes:
- Attachments included in first message: rwi_poc_scope_v1.pdf, security_questions_filled.docx (placeholders).
